description: SYNTHETIC / HAND-CONSTRUCTED QA fixtures -- known-answer backtest-engine tests (planted, computable-by-hand expected results) and pipeline QA sweeps. NONE of this is real market data; it exists to validate scripts/backtest/*, scripts/validate_composite.py and related tooling against a ground truth the owner worked out independently. Never use for research, calibration, or as a market-data source -- see docs/KNOWLEDGE.md / scripts/validate_composite.py for how these fixtures are actually consumed.
source: hand-constructed / synthetically generated by the owner's QA scripts specifically to have a known, independently computable correct backtest result -- not sourced from any exchange.
retention: permanent (these are test fixtures, not a market-data snapshot); a revision lands in a new dated/suffixed backtest_data/qa_*_<date>/ directory rather than overwriting an existing fixture, since existing tests may pin exact expected values against it.
known_defects: SYNTHETIC DATA WARNING: every file under backtest_data/qa_*/ is planted/synthetic, not observed market activity -- extreme_return, non_monotonic, crossed_book, gaps, etc. firing here reflects a deliberately constructed test scenario (e.g. a known-answer maker fill edge case), not a real data-quality defect. Do not action a hit in this dataset the way you would for a live-collected one.

some fixtures are versioned/superseded in place by name (e.g. qa_known_answer_maker3_v2_*, _v3_*, _r2_*) and at least one (qa_known_answer_maker3_v2_20260905/VOID.md) is marked void by the owner -- check for a VOID.md / superseding note in the fixture's own directory before trusting an older-looking variant.

column shapes vary per fixture (ticker/executions tape pairs, daily OHLC sweeps at different simulated cost levels, planted_values_sealed.json answer keys) -- this schema deliberately declares no `columns` and runs the full generic check suite rather than asserting a single shape across all of them.

DATA QA 2026-09-05 (docs/DATA_QA_TRIAGE.md): `quality.informational_checks: "all"` formalizes the SYNTHETIC DATA WARNING above in the schema itself rather than leaving it as prose only -- every check that fires here (duplicate_keys 60679, extreme_return 70, gaps 55593, maintenance_window 4200, split_candidate 3, zero_volume 4200 as of the 2026-09-05 report) is marked `informational: true` in QUALITY.json instead of being dropped, since the whole point of these fixtures is to keep tripping the checkers -- a future run silently returning 0 hits here would itself be the anomaly worth investigating (the fixture stopped exercising the checker it was built to exercise).
